## Anchors and geography {#sec-lingering-geo}

`{python} n_first_not_home` days start from somewhere other than *Su casa*
(`inicio_fuera_de_casa`) and `{python} n_last_not_home` do not end with a return to the home zone
(`fin_fuera_de_casa`): night shifts, second homes, nights spent elsewhere and geocoding slips all
look alike here, and nothing says which. `{python} n_first_zone_mismatch` say *Su casa* while
leaving another zone (`inicio_zona_ajena`) and no trip starts elsewhere than where the previous one
ended (`origen_discontinuo`, `{python} n_zone_breaks`): the rules of @sec-origin, @sec-copied and
@sec-rotated read them all, so only a hand edit can leave one.
`{python} pct(same_zone_share, 0)` of trips start and end in the same AGEB, which is
legitimate at this resolution and zero-distance for any skim.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-ex-geo
#| tbl-cap: "Zones and labels at odds (household 85, person 2): the day starts away from home, trip 2 was a return coded to a school in the same zone and is now Estudiar, and the last trip lands in a zone called Su casa that is not the household's."
show(person_table((85, 2)))
```

## Purposes {#sec-lingering-purpose}

`{python} fmt(len(su_casa_act))` trips carry an activity motive but a destination type of
*Su casa* (`actividad_en_casa`), `{python} fmt(su_casa_home)` of them landing in the home
zone. The ones that arrive there from another zone are returns (@sec-arrivals); most of those
left go from the home AGEB to the home AGEB, a tour whose place was never recorded, or work from
home, and are marked, not handled.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-su-casa
#| tbl-cap: "Activity motives whose destination type is 'Su casa'."
sc = su_casa_tbl.rename("trips").reset_index(); sc.columns = ["motive", "trips"]
show(sc)
```

The person in @tbl-ex-sucasa is `{python} label(ex_su_casa_work)`.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-ex-sucasa
#| tbl-cap: "A work trip that ends at Su casa in the home zone. Read as work from home, the day has a work episode at the home zone; read as a mislabelled return, it has none."
show(person_table(ex_su_casa_work))
```

The `{python} len(guard)` *Guardería* trips left (`motivo_guarderia`) are all made by children
under 12, who attend daycare, and the model reads them as school; the escorts are recoded
(@sec-daycare).

## People with no trips {#sec-zero}

`{python} n_zero_recoded` people have trip rows, every one of them a return home made from
home and marked as a non-trip (@tbl-ex-hh2). Those rows are not dropped and `viajes_contados`
still counts them, but the build sees no trips for them: they join the
`{python} fmt(said_yes_no_trips)` who said they left home and reported nothing, and all of
them look like non-travellers to a model.

## Durations and structure {#sec-lingering-structure}

The leg minutes disagree with the reported duration band on `{python} pct(band_disagree)`
of trips; the build uses the leg minutes. `{python} short_ep` activities last under five
minutes. `{python} fmt(odd_days)` people have an odd number of trips, which is normal for
a tour with two stops but also where a missing leg would show, and `{python} seven` report
exactly seven, the maximum observed. `{python} pct(minute_zero, 0)` of reported minutes
are :00.

# The hand decisions {#sec-revised}

```{python}
#| label: revised
#| include: false

decisions = chain_decisions()
n_decisions = len(decisions)
assert not decisions.duplicated(["household", "person", "trip", "field"]).any()   # one per trip and field
V = revised.trips
by_hand = V[FIX_FLAG].str.replace("minutos:revision", "", regex=False).str.contains(":revision", regex=False)
n_rows_hand = int(by_hand.sum())
n_persons_hand = int(V.index[by_hand].droplevel("folio_viaje").nunique())
n_hand_dropped = len(clean.trips.index.difference(V.index))
revised_tbl = pd.DataFrame({
    "problemas code": list(ISSUE_CODES),
    "group": ["breaking" if c in BREAKING_ISSUES else "tolerated" for c in ISSUE_CODES],
    "after the rules": [fmt(has_code(clean.trips[ISSUE_FLAG], c).sum()) for c in ISSUE_CODES],
    "after the hand decisions": [fmt(has_code(V[ISSUE_FLAG], c).sum()) for c in ISSUE_CODES],
})
assert all(int(has_code(V[ISSUE_FLAG], c).sum()) == 0 for c in BREAKING_ISSUES)
assert V.groupby(level=P).tipo_lugar_origen.nunique().max() == 1      # the day-start answer, one per person
assert tasha.validate_all(*tasha.build(revised)) == []
n_answers = int((decisions.field == "orig. type").sum())
assert (decisions.loc[decisions.field == "orig. type", "trip"] == 0).all()    # a decision about the person
assert set(decisions.source) == {"chain_review_15"}                            # one round made them all
n_hand_starts = int((decisions.field == "start").sum())
n_hand_persons = int(decisions[["household", "person"]].drop_duplicates().shape[0])

# the chain the model reads: load_eod()'s tables without the non-trips, the days counted past midnight
vt = V[~non_trips(V)].sort_index()
M = with_helpers(vt, revised.viv, revised.legs)
M_abs = M.start + 1440 * days_past_midnight(vt).to_numpy()
flags_m = day_flags(M)
per_day_m = flags_m.groupby(level=P).any()
group_share_m = {g: float(per_day_m[cols].any(axis=1).mean()) for g, cols in groups.items()}
any_share_m = float(per_day_m.any(axis=1).mean())
buildable_m = ~per_day_m[["first trip not from 'Su casa'", "last trip not a return to the home zone"]].any(axis=1)
assert not per_day_m[["does not start where the previous trip ended", "same minute as the previous trip"]].any().any()
buildable_share_m = float(buildable_m.mean())
act_m = M[~M.is_return & (M.pos < M.n)]
dur_m = (M_abs.groupby(level=P).shift(-1) - M_abs - M.legmin).reindex(act_m.index)
assert (dur_m >= 0).all()                                       # no overlap is left
zero_ep_m = float((dur_m == 0).mean())
work_dur_m = dur_m[act_m.motivo_viaje == "Trabajar"]
zero_work_m = float((work_dur_m == 0).mean())
work_median_h_m = float(work_dur_m.median() / 60)
work_6_12_m = float(((work_dur_m >= 360) & (work_dur_m <= 720)).mean())
n_zero_recoded_m = int(non_trips(V).groupby(level=P).all().sum())
```

Everything above is counted on the chain rules' output, `load_eod(revise_chains=False)`.
`load_eod()` goes on to apply the hand decisions in `eodgdl/revisions/chains.csv.gz`, merged
there from a review sheet (`eodgdl.review`) and applied in one pass: one decision per trip and
field, each made against the rules' output, with its reason, and the person's answer to where
the day started as a decision about the person (trip 0, `{python} n_answers` of them). (The
travel minutes the review corrected are not among them: the rules read them, so they go in
before the rules, @sec-minutes.) The table holds `{python} fmt(n_decisions)` decisions on
`{python} fmt(n_hand_persons)` people, all made by one review round, round 15
(`scripts/revisions/chains_15.py`, whose criteria the README there details). The rules of the
fourth review of the chains had turned the first hand pass into rules, and those of the fifth
turned two of round 14's criteria into rules too (@sec-rotated, @sec-short), read the minutes
before the rules and held a day read past midnight to hold together (@sec-night); each time every
earlier decision was retired and one round made again, from the same inputs, what still says
something the rules do not: the decisions of passes 2–6 on fields other than the start, where the
rules' output still holds the value each was made against (pass 5's rotated first trips the rule
does not read, pass 4's staff bus, pass 2's night shifts outside the rule's signature); and the
start times of every day the rules leave overlapping or the earlier tables read otherwise,
`{python} fmt(n_hand_starts)` of them, taking among the rules' reading, the earlier tables' and the
fewest minutes moved in all the one with no overlap and the fewest problems (@sec-scheduler). On
the tables the decisions give, `{python} fmt(n_rows_hand)` rows of `{python} fmt(n_persons_hand)`
people hold a value set by hand (a `<field>:revision` code in `ajustes`), `{python} n_hand_dropped`
rows the rules kept are gone — on the night-shift days the rule does not reach, the next morning's
return, outside the survey day — and no breaking code is left (@tbl-revised). TASHA cannot
schedule a trip that starts before the previous one arrives, so every overlap is breaking.
`load_eod` checks every decision against the rules' output, so a change to the rules that moves a
value a decision was made against fails the load instead of being overwritten;
`load_stages(skip_stale=True)` sets such decisions aside, `eodgdl review export --stale` puts them
on a sheet to decide again, and `eodgdl review snapshot` and `export --since` find the values a
rule change moves where no decision holds them.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-revised
#| tbl-cap: "The `problemas` codes after the chain rules and after the hand decisions, over every trip row. A breaking code leaves the chain inconsistent and is resolved by hand; a tolerated one leaves a consistent chain and is left for the consumer."
show(revised_tbl)
```

# Implications for an activity scheduler {#sec-scheduler}

A scheduler such as TASHA is estimated from whole person-days: episode frequencies by
activity type and person type, start-time and duration distributions, and the locations of
non-mandatory activities. One defect can spoil a day's episode sequence, so the person-day
is the right unit to judge the damage. The model is built from the tables `load_eod()`
returns — the rules and the hand decisions (@sec-revised) — so those are the ones that count;
the rules' output alone is shown beside them.

| person-days | after the rules | on `load_eod()`'s tables |
|---|---|---|
| any start-time defect or overnight day | `{python} pct(group_share["time"])` | `{python} pct(group_share_m["time"])` |
| any anchor or geography defect | `{python} pct(group_share["anchor / geography"])` | `{python} pct(group_share_m["anchor / geography"])` |
| any purpose ambiguity | `{python} pct(group_share["purpose"])` | `{python} pct(group_share_m["purpose"])` |
| any of the above | `{python} pct(any_share)` | `{python} pct(any_share_m)` |
| **monotone, continuous and home-to-home** | **`{python} pct(buildable_share)`** | **`{python} pct(buildable_share_m)`** |

: What the residual defects cost in person-days. On `load_eod()`'s tables the time defects left are the days that pass midnight and the late returns heaped on 23:01; no trip overlaps the one before it. {#tbl-days}

At the episode level, the rules' output alone gives `{python} pct(neg_ep)` of the activities
followed by another trip a negative duration, and `{python} pct(neg_work)` of work episodes;
on `load_eod()`'s tables none is negative, and `{python} pct(zero_ep_m)` last no minutes
(`{python} pct(zero_work_m)` of work episodes), the price of closing an overlap at the
arrival. The work-duration distribution is otherwise healthy: median
`{python} f"{work_median_h_m:.1f}"` hours, with `{python} pct(work_6_12_m, 0)` between 6 and 12
hours. Structural defects rise with the complexity of the day — after the rules,
`{python} pct(by_n[2])` of two-trip days, `{python} pct(by_n[4])` of four-trip days,
`{python} pct(by_n[6])` of six-trip days — so any filter thins the complex days a little.

**By model component.**

- *Episode durations and start times* absorb the time defects. No episode is negative on the
  model's tables; the stays of no minutes can be floored at a minute or dropped from duration
  estimation. The `{python} fmt(counts["start_times_edited"])` repaired hours and the
  `{python} fmt(counts["starts_at_arrival"])` starts moved to the arrival are the most
  economical readings of a contradiction, not observations, the
  `{python} fmt(n_untimed)` imputed start times are a neighbour's, and the hand decisions are
  readings too; `ajustes` marks them all, and an estimation that wants only observed times can
  drop those rows. The survey reports `{python} pct(minute_zero, 0)` of minutes as :00, so
  these distributions are coarse regardless.
- *Home-based tour structure* is what the scheduler assumes. The
  `{python} pct(group_share_m["anchor / geography"])` of days that do not start and end at home
  are mostly night shifts and stays elsewhere; dropping them from estimation is standard and
  cheap, and under-represents overnight work.
- *Episode frequencies by type* are barely touched. A 'Guardería' trip from age 12 is an
  escort (F) — `load_eod` recodes it (@sec-daycare) and the build reads the age the same way —
  and does not make its traveller a student; under 12 it stays school.
- *The no-travel probability* is inflated by the `{python} n_zero_recoded_m` people whose every
  row is a marked non-trip, on top of the survey's own `{python} fmt(said_yes_no_trips)`; a
  fraction of a point on a 9% base.
- *Location choice* is the least affected: the intrazonal share is a resolution property and
  the zone mismatches touch a fraction of a percent of trips. The 38 locality ids that do
  not join the AGEB census table matter more, since those destinations carry no attributes.
- *Mode choice* is trip-level and essentially unaffected.

**What limits the scheduler more than the errors.** The questionnaire elicits out-and-back
pairs: `{python} pct(pure_share, 0)` of days are pure activity-then-return sequences and
`{python} pct(share_two, 0)` of travellers report exactly two trips, so intermediate stops
and chaining — what a scheduler is meant to reproduce — are thinly observed. There is one
weekday per person, no weekend day, and a reference day a quarter of respondents place
elsewhere in the week. Activity durations are inferred from consecutive trip starts minus
travel time; the survey never asks arrival or departure times. Ages under 6 have no rows, so
escort activities lose their object. And income is unknown for 58% of households, which
weakens any segmentation the scheduler needs.

# Recommendations {#sec-recommendations}

| problem | status | recommendation | where |
|---|---|---|---|
| chain order vs start-time order | fixed | keep the row order as the sequence: `folio_viaje` is a generated number, but zones and times pin the same order; never re-sort by time or re-sequence tours | done in the contract |
| untimed trips and their duplicates | fixed | impute: the duplicate's answers where one follows, else the nearest timed trips' vote and a start counted back from the next trip; imputed rows marked `hora:…`, `motivo:…`; the duplicate row is dropped, the only row `load_eod` removes | `load_eod` |
| returns home made from home | fixed | keep the row, mark it `regreso_en_casa`; the build leaves it out | `load_eod` |
| a night shift's next-morning return | fixed | keep the row, mark it `regreso_dia_siguiente`: the day ends at work (@sec-nightshift) | `load_eod` |
| "return home" that did not reach home | fixed | recode from the destination type, zone-guarded; home where the destination copies the origin (`destino:copia`); the motive of the place where the person's trips or answer give one (`motivo:lugar`); home as the day's last trip to an AGEB nothing else touches, else 'Otros' (`destino:casa`, `motivo:otros`, @sec-short) | `load_eod` |
| activity trips that arrive home | fixed | a return (`motivo:casa`, @sec-arrivals) | `load_eod` |
| mistyped start hours | fixed | fewest-edits typo search, a second menu with the morning typed as evening, unique readings only, at least half an hour at work or school, edited rows marked `hora:+12h` and so on; the residual marked `hora_invertida` | `load_eod` |
| night shifts read as short evening stints | fixed | a return home before 10:00 after an evening trip to work is the next morning's (`hora_nocturna`, @sec-clock) | `load_eod` |
| a night read before another workday | fixed | a day read past midnight must hold together after it: no trip to work or school after the night, less than 24 hours long; the search reads the rest otherwise, a split shift as a split shift (@sec-night) | `load_eod` |
| knowing what was changed and what is left | fixed | every change on the row in `ajustes`, every defect left in `problemas`; filter with `has_code`, drop non-trips with `non_trips` | `load_eod` |
| a trip that starts elsewhere than the previous one ended | fixed | the origin is the previous destination, home after a return home (`origen:casa`, `origen:anterior`; @sec-origin) | `load_eod` |
| a first trip that copies home away | fixed | the day started at home where the origin copies the destination's AGEB, the answer says home or copies the destination's type, and the answer becomes 'Su casa'; a day that opens with a return from elsewhere answers where it started (@sec-copied); a first trip recorded from a place to home whose next trip leaves home went there from home (@sec-rotated) | `load_eod` |
| starts before the previous arrival by minutes | fixed | the start moves to the previous arrival (`hora:llegada`; @sec-arrival), within the tolerance always and up to an hour where no reading of the hours fits, not after work or school; the search runs once more where the move cleared the way | `load_eod` |
| a day that starts in the small hours with a long stay | fixed | the typo search reads it too (@sec-early); the early starts it leaves are marked `hora_madrugada` | `load_eod` |
| residual non-monotone times | fixed by hand | round 15 reads every `hora_invertida` the rules leave, which TASHA cannot schedule, by the reading with no overlap and the fewest problems among the rules', the earlier tables' and the fewest minutes moved (@sec-revised); what is left crosses midnight (`hora_nocturna`), which the model build codes past 2400 so every chain runs forward | `eodgdl/revisions/`, `tasha.build` |
| the first hand pass | retired | taken as a suggestion only: its templates became rules, its readings are one candidate in round 15's, and its decisions and notes left the table (2026-09-26) | `eodgdl.chains`, `eodgdl/revisions/` |
| leg minutes too long for the distance | fixed | a motorised trip reporting twice the survey's typical minutes for its mode and distance band takes the typical minutes (round 9's corrections), read before the rules, which read the minutes (@sec-minutes) | `eodgdl/revisions/leg_minutes.csv.gz`, `load_eod` |
| days not home-based | open | drop from scheduler estimation; keep for mode choice; night shifts keep the evening trip to work and mark the next morning's return (@sec-nightshift); the days are marked `inicio_fuera_de_casa` or `fin_fuera_de_casa` | estimation |
| Guardería coded as school | fixed | from age 12 a Guardería trip is an escort: `load_eod` recodes it 'Llevar o recoger a alguien' (`motivo:guarderia`, @sec-daycare) and the model build reads the age the same way; under 12 it stays school, marked `motivo_guarderia` | `load_eod`, `mappings.yaml` |
| people whose every row is a marked non-trip | open | drop the `{python} n_zero_recoded_m` people from estimation rather than count them as non-travellers | estimation |
| activities typed *Su casa* | decided | the ones arriving home from elsewhere are returns (@sec-arrivals); the ones from the home AGEB to the home AGEB stay activities in the home zone; marked `actividad_en_casa` | `load_eod` |
| late returns heaped on 23:01 | open | the return came at 23:01 or later; marked `hora_2301`; treat the evening activity's end as censored in estimation | estimation |
| returns heaped 1h01 and 5h01 after the trip they mirror | open | a capture default like 23:01: 767 and 682 consecutive mirrored pairs start exactly so far apart, against about 40 at the neighbouring gaps; not yet marked (found 2026-09-26) | `load_eod` |
| unjoined locality zones | open | attach attributes or map them to the nearest AGEB | zone system |
| instrument design (tours, one weekday, no durations, ages 6+, income) | inherent | state as limitations of the estimated scheduler; consider a supplementary diary | documentation |

: Every problem in this note, with where its fix lives. {#tbl-recs}

# Appendix: reproducing this note {.unnumbered}

```python
from eodgdl import load_stages, clean_trip_chains, tasha

from eodgdl._resources import leg_minutes

raw, clean, revised = load_stages()          # as shipped; the rules applied (trips gains ajustes and
                                             # problemas); then the hand decisions in eodgdl/revisions/
                                             # — what load_eod returns with clean_chains=False,
                                             # revise_chains=False and by default, from one read
trips, counts = clean_trip_chains(raw.trips, raw.viv, raw.legs, raw.hab,   # the rules on their own, with the
                                  minutes=leg_minutes())                  # minutes a review corrected first
od = tasha.build(clean)                      # the model tables, without the marked non-trips
tasha.validate_all(*od)                      # [] — the contract holds
tasha.chain_report(od.trips)                 # what remains, as counts
```

The rules and their evidence are the docstrings of `clean_trip_chains` and, stage by stage,
`_correct_minutes` (the minutes read first); `_impute_untimed_trips` (with `_duplicate_returns` and `_nearest_donors`);
`_recode_returns_by_destination`, `_returns_copying_origin`, `_arrivals_home`,
`_daycare_escorts`; `_home_to_home_returns`, `_returns_elsewhere`, `_next_morning_returns`
(`_mark_non_trips`); `_start_where_previous_ended`, `_first_origins_at_home`,
`_rotated_first_trips`, `_first_return_answers`, `_short_returns`; `_read_start_times`, with
`_repair_start_times` (`_search_edits`), `_start_at_arrival` and `_day_wraps` (`_next_day`), in
`src/eodgdl/chains.py`. The recode table is
`_MOTIVO_POR_TIPO_LUGAR_DESTINO`, the matcher's features `_IMPUTE_WEIGHTS`, the edit menus
`_START_TIME_EDITS` and `_START_TIME_EDITS_2`, the early-start thresholds `_EARLY_START` and
`_EARLY_LONG_STAY`, and the flag vocabulary `FIX_CODES` and `ISSUE_CODES` in the same file. The survey's design is described in
`data/Informe_Tecnico_Final_EOD_2023.pdf`, pp. 17–25 and 35–37.
